subject: English
central_question: How do remembrance, sacrifice, courage, leadership and responsible expression help a nation honour its bravehearts?
in_scope_units: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers—letters, school visit and the National War Memorial.
The cost of freedom, sacrifice, gallantry and gratitude.
Memorial tablets, circles and stories of fallen heroes.
Lance Naik Albert Ekka, Major Padmapani Acharya and educational resources.
Letter form, prefixes, bravery vocabulary, clauses and conjunctions.
Listening and writing about Armed Forces service in war and peace.
My Dear Soldiers—vigilance, terrain, sacrifice, prayer and service.
Imagery, simile, metaphor, repetition, alliteration, tone and theme.
Recitation, collocations, acrostic poetry and gratitude notes.
Rani Abbakka—sovereignty, refusal of tribute and resistance.
Cause and effect, comic-strip form, dialogue and inference.
Direct and indirect speech, spelling and silent letters.
Rani Gaidinliu and women who helped shape India's identity.
banned_topics: Detailed military tactics or weapon instructions.
Current political debate beyond the source.
Complete military history of every conflict or award.
External biographies not needed for the unit.

known_pitfalls.correction: The text presents remembrance, gratitude and the pain and cost of war.
The textbook note says it refers to all soldiers, men and women.

known_pitfalls.claim: Rani Abbakka misunderstands the tribute demand.
known_pitfalls.correction: She deliberately asserts Ullal's sovereignty and rejects Portuguese authority.
The unit connects courage with discipline, leadership, service and responsibility.

known_pitfalls.claim: Indirect speech needs no grammatical change.
known_pitfalls.correction: Pronouns, tense and time or place expressions often change.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with the National War Memorial and the purpose of remembrance.
Analyse one soldier's story and the language of gratitude.
Use My Dear Soldiers for theme and poetic devices.
Use Rani Abbakka for sovereignty, leadership and cause-effect.
Finish with reported speech, recitation, writing and Rani Gaidinliu.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The unit includes comprehension, extract-based reflection, poetry, vocabulary, grammar, listening, recitation, letters, acrostics and dialogue activities.
